title: nvsh bash hook + agent on error

claims.text: nvsh elevates your existing bash into a self-healing NVIDIA shell: install one sourced hook, keep bash exactly as it is, and when a command fails an NVIDIA-opinionated agent (Pi.dev driving the local associate model by default) appears inline with a diagnosis and a proposed fix you approve, retry and verify; /ask, /fix, /doctor and Ctrl+G reach the same agent on demand, and successful commands never pay a millisecond for it.

honesty_conditions.text: On spark, thor and orin, 'nvsh setup' then a normal session shows no visible change on successful commands, and 'ls /nope' produces the inline panel with the real 'No such file or directory' text in its context (--show-context).

claims.instruction: Verify end to end on the Spark in Ghostty and on orin over ssh, orin both with and without tmux: 'nvsh setup', a successful command shows nothing new, 'ls /nope' shows the panel with the real error slice, /doctor and Ctrl+G reach the agent, 'nvsh uninstall' restores the shell.

claims.text: Architecture: nvsh HOOKS into the operator's existing bash instead of wrapping it. 'nvsh install bash' appends one 'source ~/.local/share/nvsh/bash.sh' line to ~/.bashrc, the sourced file appends to the PROMPT_COMMAND array (bash>=5.1; this Spark runs 5.2.21, verified) without clobbering an existing PROMPT_COMMAND, and 'nvsh uninstall' removes it. This flips CLAUDE.md:111-120 and QWEN.md:43-45, which currently record a PTY-wrapper-as-login-shell decision.

Zero cost on the success path: the sourced bash hook is a pure-bash function that reads $? and PIPESTATUS, applies the cheap trigger pre-filter (0, 130, 141, empty line, leading-space/ignored history) in bash, and only execs the Python entrypoint when a failure qualifies. Measured on this Spark: the uv-tool entrypoint costs ~45 ms (associate --help 0.051 s, nvsh --help 0.043 s), which is too much to pay on every prompt but fine on a failure.

honesty_conditions.text: Sourcing the hook and running 1000 successful commands in 'bash --norc -i' forks no nvsh process (strace -f -e execve count of nvsh == 0) and adds < 5 ms median to prompt latency.

claims.text: Trigger rules are a table-tested pure-Python module (nvsh/triggers.py) consulted by the entrypoint before any agent call: 130, 141, grep/diff exit 1, false, test/[ ], commands run inside scripts, pipelines without pipefail (PIPESTATUS is passed in by the hook), interactive/long-running programs, plus a rate limit. Pattern triggers for exit-0 failures are opt-in.

honesty_conditions.text: tests/test_triggers.py is table-driven over (command, exit, PIPESTATUS, interactive-program flag, rate state) and covers every rule in CLAUDE.md's trigger list; all non-error rows produce 'no call'.

claims.text: Slash commands (/ask /fix /explain /retry /doctor /context /agent /help) are routed inside the same bash session by binding Enter (C-m) to a readline macro that first runs a bind -x function then accept-line (C-j). The function inspects READLINE_LINE: a line whose first word is a registered slash command is rewritten to a hidden `nvsh slash <line>` call prefixed with one space (so HISTCONTROL ignorespace keeps it out of history) and the original line is pushed with 'history -s'. Unregistered '/foo', absolute paths, quoted multi-line input and plain commands pass through unchanged. Verified in a throwaway bash 5.2 under script(1) on the Spark: /doctor and '/ask why is memory high?' routed, /notacmd and 'ls -d /tmp' ran as bash, a quoted two-line echo (Enter inside the quotes) continued normally. command_not_found_handle does NOT fire for '/doctor', so this rebind is required.

honesty_conditions.text: In an interactive Ghostty session on the Spark with Ghostty's own integration loaded: /doctor routes, 'history' shows '/doctor' and not the dispatch line, '/tmp/x' runs as a path, 'echo "a<Enter>b"' continues, and no visible flicker or duplicated prompt appears.

In an interactive Ghostty session on the Spark with Ghostty's own integration loaded: /doctor routes, 'history' shows '/doctor' and not the dispatch line, '/tmp/x' runs as a path, a quoted two-line echo (Enter pressed inside the quotes) continues, and no visible flicker or duplicated prompt appears.

claims.text: Agent boundary: nvsh/agent/ defines a small NvshAgent contract (request kinds failure|slash|explicit, streamed events text-delta|tool-call|proposal|status|done|error, cancel, capabilities) with a FakeAgent for tests and PiAgent as the default. PiAgent spawns 'pi --mode rpc' (pi 0.84.2 installed, JSONL over stdio with prompt/abort/get_state/switch_session commands and message_update/tool_execution_* events, documented in the shipped docs/rpc.md) as one long-lived subprocess per shell session so a failure does not pay pi's ~0.35 s node startup each time.

honesty_conditions.text: nvsh/agent/ imports nothing from pi; FakeAgent drives the full failure -> proposal -> approve -> retry -> verify loop in tests without pi installed; PiAgent's rpc reader splits on LF only and handles abort and a killed pi process without hanging the shell.

claims.text: Deterministic nvsh tools (inspect_gpu, inspect_memory, inspect_containers, inspect_services, read_logs, retry_command, verify) are implemented once in Python. To expose them to Pi as first-class tools, nvsh ships one generic TypeScript extension file loaded via `pi -e <path>` that forwards each call to `nvsh tool <name> --json`; pi has no RPC command to register tools from outside the process (verified in docs/extensions.md and docs/rpc.md). Mutating proposals surface as 'proposal' events and are confirmed by the operator in nvsh, mirroring shell-cli's operations.py apply=False default and deny-wins policy. (Per decision c25, v1 uses only pi's bash tool; the extension shim is the later migration path.)

honesty_conditions.text: No agent-proposed command ever runs without an explicit operator keypress; the audit log records every proposal, the decision and the outcome; the fixture test asserts a 'sudo rm -rf' proposal is shown but never executed.

hard_questions.text: Shipping a TypeScript pi extension inside a Python package: acceptable for v1 so nvsh tools are first-class pi tools, or should v1 give pi only a prompt plus the 'bash' RPC tool and keep all tool execution on the nvsh side?
hard_questions.resolution: v1 gives pi only the prompt and its built-in bash tool (no TypeScript shim). nvsh skills and resident deterministic tools are explored first inside the associate harness (~/git/associate), then migrated into nvsh once they prove out.

'exec > >(tee)' is rejected because it breaks isatty and colors.

hard_questions.text: Is re-running the failed command under script(1) acceptable as the default way to capture its output for diagnosis (it re-executes side effects), or should v1 only diagnose from exit code + command line unless the session is inside tmux?
hard_questions.resolution: nvsh never re-runs a failed command silently. It first diagnoses from exit code, command line, PIPESTATUS and machine context; if output is needed it asks the operator before re-running under script(1), because the command may have side effects. Ghostty gives OSC 133 prompt/command markers, not a programmatic read of the scrollback, so it does not replace this rule.

claims.text: Output capture rule: diagnose first from exit status, command line, PIPESTATUS and machine context; ask before any re-run under script(1); use tmux capture-pane only when already inside tmux. No silent re-execution ever.

'nvsh setup' installs the capture layer along with pi and the hooks: a per-session typescript via util-linux script(1) (present on spark, thor, orin) started from the hook file when the shell is interactive, not already under script or tmux, and not nested; tmux is installed/used when the operator wants a multiplexer (orin lacks it; apt candidate 3.4) and then tmux pipe-pane is the log source instead. Either log is sliced per command by Ghostty's OSC 133 C/D markers, which nvsh's hook file re-sources from /usr/share/ghostty/shell-integration/bash/ghostty.bash when TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty (or emits itself elsewhere). So the failed command's actual output is available without any re-run; re-run stays ask-first.

hard_questions.text: One pi process per shell (isolation, but N terminals = N node processes; impossible on orin and heavy on a 3 GB-free Jetson) or one per user with pi's steer/follow-up queue serialising concurrent failures from several terminals (shared 1M context across terminals, which the 'this worked this morning' use case in issue #2 actually wants)?
hard_questions.resolution: Single pi session per user by default, configurable to more. When a different shell session sends work, the current conversation is put to sleep (saved) and a fresh one serves the new shell, so contexts from different terminals never mix; a sleeping conversation resumes when its shell returns.

obligations.behavior: a line whose first word is a registered slash command routes to 'nvsh slash' with the original line in history; every other line passes through unchanged
obligations.source_text: Slash commands (/ask /fix /explain /retry /doctor /context /agent /help) are routed inside the same bash session by binding Enter (C-m) to a readline macro that first runs a bind -x function then accept-line (C-j). The function inspects READLINE_LINE: a line whose first word is a registered slash command is rewritten to a hidden `nvsh slash <line>` call prefixed with one space (so HISTCONTROL ignorespace keeps it out of history) and the original line is pushed with 'history -s'. Unregistered '/foo', absolute paths, quoted multi-line input and plain commands pass through unchanged. Verified in a throwaway bash 5.2 under script(1) on the Spark: /doctor and '/ask why is memory high?' routed, /notacmd and 'ls -d /tmp' ran as bash, a quoted two-line echo (Enter inside the quotes) continued normally. command_not_found_handle does NOT fire for '/doctor', so this rebind is required.

The panel renders with hard-coded SGR sequences guarded by NO_COLOR / TERM=dumb / non-tty checks and never calls tput; 'nvsh doctor' detects missing terminfo and prints the 'infocmp -x | ssh host tic -x -' remediation.

obligations.behavior: routing, Ctrl+G and the palette work in emacs mode and after 'set -o vi'
obligations.source_text: Readline keymaps: the Enter macro, Ctrl+G and the palette are bound in the emacs, vi-insert and vi-command keymaps (one 'bind -m' per keymap); probe on the Spark showed a plain 'bind -x' binding does not fire after 'set -o vi' while a vi-insert keymap binding does.

obligations.behavior: a LAN endpoint is probed with a timeout; an unreachable or absent endpoint yields a clear message and never a hang
obligations.source_text: The default model is LAN-local, not on-box: Pi's 'associate' is served by a gateway on 192.168.1.138, and orin (no node, 3.1 GB MemAvailable) cannot host pi or a model. So 'offline-first' in v1 means 'no internet, LAN reachable'; a truly air-gapped machine needs an on-box endpoint configured or gets 'no agent configured' from doctor with a clear message, never a hang.

obligations.behavior: argv contains --no-context-files --no-extensions --no-skills --no-prompt-templates --no-approve and a session flag; no file appears under ~/.pi/agent/sessions after a run
obligations.source_text: pi launch hygiene: PiAgent starts pi with --no-context-files (otherwise pi reads CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md from the user's cwd into the prompt), --no-extensions, --no-skills, --no-prompt-templates, --no-approve, and either --no-session or --session-dir under $XDG_STATE_HOME/nvsh (0700). Probe: pi stores sessions per cwd under ~/.pi/agent/sessions (26 project dirs on the Spark), so an unflagged run would persist redacted-but-sensitive failure context into project-named session files.

obligations.behavior: ssh, docker exec, kubectl exec, tmux, screen, su and sudo -i never auto-trigger; /fix still works on them
obligations.source_text: Remote and container commands are pass-through for triggers: 'ssh host cmd', 'docker exec -it', 'kubectl exec', tmux/screen attach and 'su'/'sudo -i' return the remote or inner status, which is not this machine's failure. The trigger table lists them as never-auto-trigger; the operator can still /fix them explicitly.

obligations.behavior: no nvsh or pi process at shell start; one daemon after the first qualifying failure; none after the last shell exits; one-shot fallback when the daemon is missing
obligations.source_text: Warm-session ownership: the long-lived pi process is owned by an nvsh session daemon started lazily on the first qualifying failure (never at shell start), listening on a per-user socket under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nvsh/; the 45 ms hook client connects, streams the panel, and exits. The daemon dies on an idle timeout and when its last shell exits (EXIT trap sends a stop); stale sockets are reaped at the next start. If the daemon or pi is missing or crashed, the client falls back to a one-shot 'pi -p' run so a failure is never left without a diagnosis.

obligations.seam: hook file version stamp vs nvsh --version
obligations.behavior: an older stamp prints the refresh notice once per session; 'nvsh setup' re-renders and the notice stops
obligations.source_text: Upgrade path: the sourced ~/.local/share/nvsh/bash.sh carries the nvsh version that rendered it; the failure-path client compares it with its own version and prints 'run nvsh setup to refresh the hook' once per session when they differ. 'nvsh setup' is idempotent and re-renders; a 'uv tool upgrade nvsh' alone never breaks the shell because the old hook only calls stable verbs.

obligations.behavior: NVSH_DISABLE=1 yields no hook, no bindings and no capture; off/on unbind and rebind; uninstall leaves the rc byte-identical to the backup and no files, sockets or processes
obligations.source_text: Kill switch and reversibility: NVSH_DISABLE=1 in the environment makes the sourced file a no-op; 'nvsh off' / 'nvsh on' unbind and rebind Enter, the palette and the hook in the current shell; 'nvsh uninstall' removes the marked block from ~/.bashrc (restoring from its backup if the block was edited), the hook file, runtime sockets and logs, and stops daemons. Hook functions never use set -e and end with '|| return 0'. Probe on the Spark: an erroring bind -x function still lets the Enter macro accept the line, so a bug degrades, it does not lock the terminal.

obligations.behavior: Ctrl+C aborts the run and returns a working prompt within 1 s; /fix still finds the last failure; killing script(1) or the daemon leaves the shell usable
obligations.source_text: Interrupt and cleanup: Ctrl+C while the panel is streaming sends rpc abort to pi, restores the terminal and returns to a clean prompt with the original failure still available to /fix; killing script(1) or the daemon mid-session leaves the shell usable; stale session logs under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nvsh are removed at next setup or shell start.

obligations.behavior: a 5 MB binary failure yields at most 64 KB with a truncation marker, valid UTF-8, no escape sequences, redacted; the log path never appears in the request
obligations.source_text: The output slice sent to the agent is bounded (last 64 KB of the failed command's C..D region, head+tail with a marker when truncated), handled as bytes with invalid UTF-8 replaced, stripped of escape sequences before redaction, and redacted before it leaves the hook client. The session log itself is never transmitted whole and never leaves the machine.

obligations.behavior: no auto-apply code path exists; a 'sudo apt install x' proposal is shown verbatim, requires Enter, and is never inserted into READLINE_LINE
obligations.source_text: No auto-apply in v1: every proposal, including package installs and container stops, waits for an explicit keypress; there is no 'safe auto-fix policy' switch yet, and 'sudo' proposals are shown with the exact command and never pre-typed into the prompt.

obligations.behavior: hook_sourced, hook_first_in_prompt_command, bindings_present, capture_active, daemon_status, terminfo_present each report pass/fail with a remediation; ordering fails when the hook is last
obligations.source_text: 'nvsh doctor' gains in-shell checks with remediations: hook file sourced, nvsh hook first in PROMPT_COMMAND, Enter/Tab/Ctrl+G bindings present in the active keymap, capture active (script or tmux pipe-pane) with the log path and mode, daemon and pi status, harness reachable, terminfo present; '/doctor' prints the same inline.

obligations.behavior: fnmatch on the full command line; add() refuses sudo, rm and bare patterns; defaults present; session list in memory only; every allowlisted run audited
obligations.source_text: Approval allowlists: 'approved for user' lives at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nvsh/approved.toml (0600) as glob patterns matched against the full command line with fnmatch semantics; 'approved for session' lives in the daemon's memory and dies with it. Defaults ship read-only inspectors ('nvidia-smi *', 'docker ps*', 'journalctl *', 'systemctl status *', 'df *', 'free *', 'nvsh *') and never 'sudo *', 'rm *' or a bare '*'; 'nvsh approve list/add/remove' and '/approve' manage them; every allowlisted execution is still written to the audit log.

obligations.behavior: failures from shells A and B stay in separate conversations, one pi process serves both, sleeping conversations resume, sessions.max raises the limit
obligations.source_text: Session daemon model (from decision on q9): one nvsh daemon and one pi process per user, $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nvsh/daemon.sock; each shell session (keyed by the hook's shell PID) owns its own pi conversation. When a request arrives from a shell other than the active one, the daemon puts the active conversation to sleep (pi rpc switch_session / new_session, which persist to the nvsh-owned session dir) and activates the caller's conversation, resuming it on its next request. 'sessions.max' in config allows more concurrent pi processes for machines that can afford them.

obligations.behavior: drops the last agent turn and its proposal; the executor is never called
obligations.source_text: /undo in v1 rewinds the agent conversation (last turn and its proposal) and never reverts machine changes; reverting changes is a follow-up tracked as a GitHub issue on agentculture/nvsh.
